name: Eman Zied
bio:
Dr Eman Zeid PhD is a Research Fellow affiliated with the Addressing inequity in health and care systems theme at the NIHR Applied Research Collaboration North East and North Cumbria (NIHR ARC-NENC). 
As geospatial data scientist by background, Eman has extensive expertise in the use of geographical information systems (GIS) in public health. She is primarily interested in the complex interplay between social, spatial and health inequalities, spatial determinants of health and climate as an emerging facet of inequalities. Her individual programme of work examines spatial vulnerabilities to heatwaves through a health inequalities lens, with a view to developing interventions for local authorities and healthcare practitioners.
Her research explores how the built and natural environment shapes health outcomes and influences social and health inequalities. She has worked on research projects focusing on the relationship between the environment and cognitive health, inequalities in health-related amenities on the high street and community pharmacy distribution in deprived areas. She is currently working on a career development project focusing on the prevention of hospitalisation during heatwaves, and how structural inequalities can drive health outcomes during heatwaves.
As an early career researcher, she has been awarded over £106,000 in research funding as a principal investigator and over £500,000  in collaborative grants. Her research has been featured in over 130 pieces of media, including The Guardian, The Chronicle, The Mirror, The Independent and The Pharmaceutical Journal. She has expertise in engaging with MPs, local authorities and other stakeholders. She has contributed written evidence to parliamentary inquiries, and she is currently collaborating with local authorities to develop heat plans to protect residents' health and wellbeing.
